entities.name: Aryl acid chloride
observations: Decoded reactant: CC(C)(C#N)c1cccc(C(=O)Cl)c1, an aryl acid chloride bearing a tert-cyanoalkyl substituent.
The acyl chloride carbon is the electrophilic center in the inferred amidation.

entities.name: Amino cresol
observations: Decoded reactant: CC1=CC=C(N)C=C1O, an aminomethylphenol positional isomer.
The aniline nitrogen is the nucleophile; the phenolic oxygen remains unacylated in the product.

entities.name: Aryl carboxamide product
observations: Product connectivity is consistent with replacement of acid-chloride Cl by amino-cresol N, forming an Ar-C(O)-NH-Ar amide.

entities.name: Aroyl chloride aminolysis
observations: Nucleophilic acyl substitution: the acyl C-Cl bond is replaced by an acyl C-N bond.
The reaction is aromatic amide formation from an aroyl chloride and an aniline; no catalyst or redox step is required.

entities.name: NaHCO3 THF water
observations: Close ORD precedents use sodium bicarbonate base in tetrahydrofuran and water for analogous aroyl chloride/aniline amidations.
No explicit coupling catalyst, yield, time, or temperature was returned in the cited evidence.

entities.name: Tertiary amine base alternatives
observations: Chemically plausible alternatives for HCl scavenging include triethylamine or pyridine in THF or dichloromethane, but these are not directly established by the cited ORD records.
